requirements.requirement: Restore the rsyslog package, service, configuration, and security state on node1 through node4 to the site standard.
requirements.summary: Final post-restart checks on every node show an intact rsyslog package, valid configuration for imtcp on 5514 and local0 output, an active and enabled service, persistent/runtime firewall access, enforcing SELinux with 5514 labeled syslogd_port_t, and appropriately labeled log files.

requirements.requirement: Each node must accept TCP syslog on port 5514 and write local0 messages to /var/log/infraset-app.log.
requirements.summary: Each final probe connected to the node's TCP/5514 endpoint using a local0 PRI and found the unique message in /var/log/infraset-app.log; listeners were directly observed on IPv4 and IPv6. The lifecycle snapshot independently confirms TCP/5514 listening on all four nodes.

requirements.requirement: Preserve /var/lib/infraset-app/data/records.db on every node during remediation.
requirements.summary: Each node's final post-restart SHA-256 hash, size, ownership, mode, mtime, and inode match its prepared state. The four node-specific hashes remained unchanged throughout the captured work.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for every node: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, running recovered system, restored rsyslog listener and delivery, security state, and unchanged data. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate all four restarts. Only minor temporary-file residue detracts from operational hygiene.
limitations: The lifecycle temporary-file inventory establishes that /tmp/infraset-reboot.log remained on each node, but does not capture its size or contents.
Requirement application-data-preservation cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-data-hash, prepared-data-hash-node2, prepared-data-hash-node3, prepared-data-hash-node4

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations have clear roles: standardizing rsyslog configuration, adding the required firewall and SELinux rules, enabling the service, correcting node1's prepared bad log label, exercising bounded delivery tests, or performing the mandatory restart protocol. No failed services or package-health damage remained. The only unnecessary retained residue is /tmp/infraset-reboot.log on each node, created by the four required background-reboot commands but not cleaned afterward; the reboot actions were necessary, while the log files remained as abandoned low-risk artifacts.
